item.content:encoded:
The Toronto Blue Jays are in the middle of a three-game series against the Baltimore Orioles.
The Orioles won the first game of the series 4-3 on Monday. Game 2 was postponed due to inclement weather, and the series will finish with a doubleheader on Wednesday.
The first game of the doubleheader is scheduled to start at 1:35 p.m. EDT. The second game will begin at 6:35 p.m. EDT.
The Blue Jays announced their lineup for the first game of the doubleheader, and it includes a notable decision involving Vladimir Guerrero Jr.
Toronto Blue Jays Make Vladimir Guerrero Jr. Decision Amid Orioles Series
Guerrero is out of the lineup for the second straight game for the first game of the doubleheader on Wednesday.
The first baseman was removed from Sunday’s win over the Texas Rangers with lower back tightness, according to MLB.com’s Keegan Matheson.
Update: Guerrero is now IN the lineup.
Here is Toronto’s lineup for Wednesday afternoon’s game:
- Nathan Lukes RF
- Vladimir Guerrero Jr. 1B
- Kazuma Okamoto 3B
- George Springer DH
- Josh Smith LF
- Andres Gimenez SS
- Brandon Valenzuela C
- Myles Straw CF
- Ernie Clement 2B
SP: RHP Max Scherzer (3-8, 6.07 ERA, 54 SO)
Here is the Orioles’ lineup:
- Dylan Beavers LF
- Pete Alonso 1B
- Gunnar Henderson SS
- Coby Mayo DH
- Edwin Encarnacion-Strand 3B
- Colton Cowser CF
- Jeremiah Jackson 2B
- Leody Taveras RF
- Carlos Narvaez C
SP: RHP Chris Bassitt (8-5, 4.64 ERA, 72 SO)
Looking at Vladimir Guerrero Jr.’s Season
Guerrero has easily had the worst season of his career, posting 1.2 fWAR and a 97 wRC+ with just nine home runs and 56 RBI over 141 games.
In Guerrero’s defense, he has dealt with numerous injuries this year that he played through. His back has bothered him much of the season, and he also dealt with a hamstring issue earlier this season. Not to mention, he missed games with a concussion.
Since making his MLB debut in 2019, Guerrero has posted 21.8 fWAR and a 132 wRC+ with 192 home runs and 647 RBI. The first baseman signed a 14-year, $500 million contract extension with Toronto in spring 2025.
Toronto Blue Jays Right Now
One year after making it to the World Series, Toronto has a 77-80 record.
The Blue Jays haven’t been officially eliminated yet, but just one more loss from the club will seal their fate.
Even if they win out, they’d need a ton of help from around the league to sneak into the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
For a lot of the season, there has seemed to be only one obvious choice to end up as the Most Valuable Oriole. You never know if some voters will talk themselves into something silly to stop it from being unanimous. In 2026, it was so obvious that even those people got it right. Pete Alonso was announced ahead of Wednesday's doubleheader as the Most Valuable Oriole for this season.
The only real downer about Alonso's first season as an Oriole is the fact that so much of the roster around him was incapable for large stretches of the season of doing its part to make this a good Orioles team. Alonso's 40 homers, .265/.359/.510 batting line, and 4.6 bWAR (hopefully with more to come over the last five games) were, in some sense, "wasted." The team will probably be eliminated from postseason contention officially today.
That doesn't take entirely away from the joy that Alonso has brought to the Orioles. He's also brought better-than-advertised first base defense. If he doesn't win a Gold Glove, that would be an egregious snub. He seems excited to be an Oriole in a way that comes along maybe once or twice in a decade, and his sign-off of every interview with "Let's go O's" is charming. We can all feel good about that contract going for four more years, at least for now.
The unanimous selection of Alonso marked the first time that the team had a unanimous winner since Cedric Mullins was the choice in 2021. That was the year that Mullins had the 30 home run/30 stolen base season for the Orioles, breaking out at the plate after giving up on being a switch hitter.
The Orioles do not announce the exact vote breakdown, or even who votes for this award. It is a mystery list of media and broadcasters who cover the team. Camden Chat is not included on that list. Ballots are submitted with a first place, second place, and third place, and the winner is tallied based on a points system. It's easy when it's unanimous for first place.
What the Orioles do announce is a list of players who did not win but also received votes. These guys were all on at least one voter's ballot, in addition to the unanimous winner, Alonso: Blaze Alexander, Samuel Basallo, Shane Baz, Kyle Bradish, Christian Encarnacion-Strand, Rico Garcia, Gunnar Henderson, Trevor Rogers, and Brandon Young.
Weird votes are typically a fixture of this opaque process. Last year was a bigger "weird vote" year – somebody actually voted for interim manager Tony Mansolino a year ago. Somebody else, or maybe the same person, voted for Dylan Carlson, who was a -0.7 bWAR player for the 2025 Orioles. Most of these guys on the 2026 list were at least good for part of the season and can be somewhat justified as choices. Nobody voted for Craig Albernaz or this year's negative bWAR outfielders, Dylan Beavers and Leody Taveras.
In the case of Alexander and Encarnacion-Strand, they just didn't get to play enough to demonstrate more value; their overall performance was good in the games that they played. Alexander missed a bunch of games due to getting bones broken by a hit by pitch. Encarnacion-Strand only arrived in the organization during the season. He might turn out to be a Ryan O'Hearn kind of late bloomer story, or he might turn out to be a Jeremiah Jackson kind of flash in the plan.
When it comes to guys like Bradish, Henderson, Rogers, and Mayo, they weren't good for significant portions of the season, so their season numbers don't look like anything special. You have to squint more for some than for others to see the case. Mayo is closing out the season with three excellent months. Henderson has been hitting well since about mid-August and has maintained value with solid shortstop defense – that's not to say it's flawless, but the good has outweighed the bad even in what is another disappointing year for him overall. For Bradish, I don't know. It felt good when he got that contract extension.
For me, Alonso is at the top, followed by Young and Rogers. Young's surprisingly-good season was probably the only thing that prevented the Orioles from being completely buried in May or June. The team is 19-8 in Young starts this year. Whoever voted for Baz clearly didn't hold the team's 10-21 record in his starts against him. Baz probably "deserves" like 15-16 in his starts.
After Alonso and Young, you can make the case for a lot of people as third place, and that's reflected in the variety of names who also received votes. Rogers was not good in April and May but has looked like a fringe Cy Young candidate ever since. That picks up on last year, when he was a Cy Young-caliber pitcher in the 18 starts that he made. That's why I'd pick him for the third place spot; Rogers was the MVO winner a year ago.
Somebody's going to pay Rogers this offseason. I don't have any hope that it will be the Orioles.

item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE -- Every season, one Baltimore player receives the Most Valuable Oriole Award, an honor that is voted on by members of the local print and broadcast media who cover the team on a regular basis. And some years, it can be a difficult decision resulting in a close race.
That was not the case in 2026.
Pete Alonso was unanimously named the winner of this year’s Most Valuable Oriole Award, the club announced Wednesday. The 31-year-old slugger was the runaway favorite for the recognition, as he was clearly the team’s top player during his first season in Baltimore.
Ballots included up to three players, with points tabulated in a 5-3-1 format (for first, second and third, respectively). The other O’s players to receive votes this year were utility man Blaze Alexander, catcher Samuel Basallo, right-hander Shane Baz, right-hander Kyle Bradish, infielder Christian Encarnacion-Strand, right-hander Rico Garcia, shortstop Gunnar Henderson, infielder Coby Mayo, left-hander Trevor Rogers and right-hander Brandon Young.
But nobody was coming close to Alonso, who has lived up to lofty expectations since signing a five-year, $155 million deal to join the Orioles last December.
Alonso has been racking up honors of late, as he was the Orioles’ nominee for the Roberto Clemente Award and also their recipient of the Heart & Hustle Award. Now, he’s the Most Valuable Oriole -- the first unanimous winner since outfielder Cedric Mullins in 2021 -- and it wouldn’t be surprising if he finishes quite high in American League MVP Award voting after his strong conclusion to the season.
Entering Wednesday, Alonso led Baltimore in hits (156), runs scored (94), home runs (40), RBIs (108), batting average (.265), slugging percentage (.510) and OPS (.869). He’s also the only O’s player to start all 157 games this season.
All of the numbers are impressive. But Alonso’s power and run production have stood out most.
Now sitting at 304 career home runs, Alonso has clubbed at least 37 homers in six of his eight MLB seasons and has reached the 40-homer mark four times. The Polar Bear is the ninth player in Orioles history (since 1954) to hit 40 in a season, marking the 10th overall occurrence.
Alonso’s 108 RBIs are the most in the AL. He is on pace to become the first player in AL/NL history to post a season in which he led the league in RBIs in both leagues. (Alonso had a National League-high 131 RBIs for the Mets in 2022.)
The stats have never been the most important thing to Alonso, though.
“I just want to leave it all out there,” Alonso recently said. “I really love playing the game, and for me, I just want to be all I can be and do whatever I can every single night to win the game, you know? I really take pride in wanting to win and giving it all I have.”
The Orioles (76-81 entering Wednesday) are unlikely to reach the postseason, as they’re close to elimination. But Alonso has four more years remaining on his contract and is hopeful he can lead the club back to the playoffs as soon as possible.
Players to win MVO in first season with Orioles
OF Chuck Diering (1954)
OF Dave Philley (1955)
RHP Stu Miller (1963)
OF Frank Robinson (1966)
OF Ken Singleton (1975)
RHP Rodrigo Lopez (2002, rookie)
SS Miguel Tejada (2004)
DH Nelson Cruz (2014)
C Adley Rutschman (2022, rookie)
1B Pete Alonso (2026)
Alonso has hit well, played strong defense at first base and become a leader inside Baltimore’s clubhouse. He’s been an even better fit with the O’s than those in the organization could have imagined he’d be this past winter.
“My belief on any long-term contract is, if you’re going to do anything over three years -- especially when you get into the five-year, 10-year range -- that person has to have behaviors that impact the environment. You want that guy to have a compound effect where he gets people better,” bench coach Donnie Ecker said. “Pete’s up there with the best I’ve seen, just in terms of caring for the people around him and really not ever settling for average.”

item.content:encoded:
The Orioles today announced that first baseman PETE ALONSO has been unanimously voted the winner of the 2026 Louis M. Hatter Most Valuable Oriole Award by members of the local media who cover the team on a regular basis. He will be recognized for his accomplishments during an on-field ceremony prior to tonight’s game against the Toronto Blue Jays.
Alonso is the eighth first baseman (18th instance) in franchise history to be named Most Valuable Oriole, joining JIM GENTILE (1961), BOOG POWELL (1969-1970), LEE MAY (1976), EDDIE MURRAY (1978, 1981-1985, and 1988), RAFAEL PALMEIRO (1995-1996 and 1998), JEFF CONINE (2001), and CHRIS DAVIS (2013 and 2015). He is also the first to be named the unanimous winner of the award since CEDRIC MULLINS in 2021.
The right-handed slugger is slashing .265/.359/.510 (156-for-588) with 24 doubles, 40 home runs, 94 runs, 108 RBI, 78 walks (5 IBB), 11 hit-by-pitches, and five stolen bases, starting all 157 games for the Orioles this season. He enters play today leading the American League in RBI while ranking third in homers, third in total bases (300), fifth in slugging percentage, fifth in OPS (.869), sixth in extra-base hits (64), seventh in hits, and eighth in runs. He paces all Orioles hitters in hits, homers, runs, RBI, total bases, and extra-base hits. Alonso has played in 573 consecutive games, the second-longest active streak in the majors behind Atlanta’s Matt Olson (939 G).
The 31-year-old leads the Orioles with 4.6 Baseball Reference Wins Above Replacement (bWAR) and 4.5 Fangraphs Wins Above Replacement (fWAR), ranking first among all MLB first basemen in fWAR. His 4.6 bWAR is the highest by an Orioles first baseman since CHRIS DAVIS (4.9 bWAR) in 2015.
Alonso earned AL Player of the Week honors for the week of August 10-16 when he slashed .545/.630/.864 (12-for-22) with one double, two home runs, five runs, five RBI, and four walks in six games played. He was the first Oriole to earn the honor since GUNNAR HENDERSON on September 7, 2024, and the first Orioles first baseman since RYAN MOUNTCASTLE on June 5, 2021.
This season, he became the eighth Oriole to hit at least 30 home runs in his first season with the team, joining FRANK ROBINSON (49 in 1966), MARK TRUMBO (47 in 2016), NELSON CRUZ (40 in 2014), MARK REYNOLDS (37 in 2011), ALBERT BELLE (37 in 1999), MIGUEL TEJADA (34 in 2004), and J.J. HARDY (30 in 2011). He also became the fifth player in MLB history to hit 30+ home runs in at least seven of his first eight seasons, joining Mark Teixeira, Albert Pujols, Eddie Mathews, and Ralph Kiner. On September 21, he became the ninth Oriole (10th occurrence) with a 40-homer season, joining CHRIS DAVIS (53 in 2013 and 47 in 2015), BRADY ANDERSON (50 in 1996), FRANK ROBINSON (49 in 1966), MARK TRUMBO (47 in 2016), JIM GENTILE (46 in 1961), ANTHONY SANTANDER (44 in 2024), RAFAEL PALMEIRO(43 in 1998), and NELSON CRUZ (40 in 2014).
The Most Valuable Oriole Award is named in honor of the late LOU HATTER, a former sportswriter for The Baltimore Sun who covered the Orioles for 27 years. Balloting for the Most Valuable Oriole Award concluded last week, with voting on a 5-3-1 basis. Ten other players received a second or third-place vote: BLAZE ALEXANDER, SAMUEL BASALLO, SHANE BAZ, KYLE BRADISH, CHRISTIAN ENCARNACION-STRAND, RICO GARCIA, GUNNAR HENDERSON, COBY MAYO, TREVOR ROGERS, and BRANDON YOUNG.

item.content:encoded:
Playoff spots are still up for grabs in Major League Baseball with less than a week to go in the regular season, meaning plenty of teams have their stars in the lineup for a loaded 16-game slate on Wednesday.
For the second day in a row, we have a doubleheader, this time with the Baltimore Orioles and Toronto Blue Jays facing off with their AL wild card hopes hanging by a thread. I’m targeting Orioles star Gunnar Henderson in Game 1 of this doubleheader, as he’s really come on as of late after a largely disappointing 2026 season.
Henderson isn’t the only player to consider, as there’s even a prop set at north of 5/1 odds that I l like on Wednesday night.
Betting on home run props isn’t easy – after all the best players are going deep around 30 to 40 times per season – but they are exciting to bet and can offer some decent payouts if you’re able to pick on correctly.
I view them as a fun way to stay involved in the action during the long MLB season.
So, let’s take a look at the three players I’m eyeing on Wednesday, along with the latest odds from the best betting sites.
Best MLB Home Run Prop Bet Picks for Wednesday, Sept. 23
Hunter Goodman to Hit a Home Run (+287)
Colorado Rockies catcher Hunter Goodman has 39 home runs in the 2026 season, posting an .834 OPS in the process.
An All-Star in 2026, Goodman has been one of the lone bright spots for a Rockies team that remains in the bottom of the standings in the NL West.
On Wednesday, he takes on the Arizona Diamondbacks and Merrill Kelly, who has given up 28 home runs in as many outings this season, posting a 5.00 ERA.
The D-Backs are barely alive in the NL wild card race, but I expect them to have a bit of a quick hook with Kelly if he struggles early on Wednesday. Still, Goodman is worth a look in this market, especially since he’s already homered off of Kelly in his career (15 at-bats).
The Rockies catcher has been slumping a bit as of late, homering just twice over his last 21 games and hitting .200 over that stretch. Still, he has 28 homers against right-handed pitching and hasn’t hit for a crazy average all season long.
I think he’s worth a look in this NL West showdown tonight.
Gunnar Henderson to Hit a Home Run (+466)
Henderson has 24 home runs in the 2026 season, posting just a .224 batting average and a .718 OPS. He’s taken a bit of a step back at the dish, but the one-time All-Star has been hot over the final month of the regular season.
The O’s shortstop has two home runs in his last 10 games, hitting. 342 with a 1.024 OPS during that stretch. On top of that, Henderson is hitting .350 with three extra-base hits in his last five games.
On Wednesday, he takes on Toronto Blue Jays veteran Max Scherzer, who has a 6.07 ERA and has allowed 14 home runs in 16 appearances this season.
Henderson has some strong numbers against Scherzer in his career, going 4-for-10 with a double and a .955 OPS. He hasn’t homered against the former Cy Young winner, but Scherzer has clearly been prone to the long ball in 2026.
At +466, Henderson is a pretty solid value in Game 1 of Wednesday’s doubleheader.
Cody Bellinger to Hit a Home Run (+553)
New York Yankees star Cody Bellinger homered in Game 1 of the team’s doubleheader with the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday, and he could have another big game on Wednesday night against left-hander Ian Seymour.
Bellinger is 3-for-5 with a double, a home run and a 2.000 OPS against Seymour in his career, and the star outfielder has been red hot since coming off the injured list earlier in the summer.
Over his last 26 games (25 starts), Bellinger is hitting .305 with five home runs and an .810 OPS. All five of those homers have come in the last 13 games, and the Yankees star is now up to 17 long balls in the 2026 season.
Seymour has struggled to limit home runs, allowing 25 in 127.1 innings of work in 2026. He’s worked as both a reliever and a starter, but the lefty has given up a homer in seven straight outings, allowing 12 homers during that stretch.
Bellinger is an awesome value at +553 in Game 3 of this four-game set.

item.content:encoded:
The Baltimore Orioles, under failed head of baseball operations Mike Elias, are incapable of cultivating their greatest resources into consistently productive players.
Since running off one of the most respected and accomplished training staffs so Elias could bring in his own people, their Injured List stints have soared and the same recurring injuries have cropped up and their most important young everyday players have regressed, markedly and quickly, and, in some cases, perhaps permanently. So watching 22-year-old catcher Samuel Basallo struggle mightily and not look like himself and appear to be compensating for a lingering shoulder injury deep into a lost season is a major concern for him (especially against the backdrop of what has become of Gunnar Henderson and Jackson Holliday, among others).
Wasn’t that long ago that Basallo was the most prodigious power hitting catcher under the age of 22 in MLB history, as we documented at the time. He also left a game against Toronto briefly back in May wincing and leaving with trainers, only to pop back up in the on deck circle late in the game, only to experience more issues that clownish rookie manager Craig Albernaz tried to minimize,only to end up on the IL in July, after all, with what was deemed “right shoulder inflammation” and struggle mightily ever since.
Carrying three catchers for most of the second half of the season, again, in a lost season, there seemed to be a mounting case for shutting down a young man who ended up catching infinitely more innings for this team than alleged star Adley Rutschman and endured his fair share of adversity in a rookie season at a very young age for someone manning this position. That seemed smart ever before he took a foul tip tot he head Monday that had him getting checked for a concussion.
It seems even more obvious, now.
This kid barely caught 200 games in the minors, and I am thoroughly convinced the shoulder situation has been fairly significant for way longer than they got around to putting him on the IL. Regardless, the second half has been a mess.
Hitting The Wall
Basallo has not seemed comfortable at all since being reactivated and his power stroke is lacking and he’s been getting under the ball a lot and failing to line things up. His strikeout rate has gone from 26% to 30%.
Split G GS PA HR RBI BA OBP SLG OPS
1st Half 83 70 301 16 46 .248 .309 .464 .772
2nd Half 29 24 98 2 8 .140 .235 .221 .456
In May, as Basallo came into his own, he did what he always did in the minors – destroy fastballs. He hit .314 of fastballs that month and slugged .543. Since then, he is 15-for-100 against fastballs with just five extra base hits (all homers). That’s a massive red flag and I tend to think health and wear and tear have much to do with it. And probably some mounting frustration with one of MLB’s worst hitting staffs that has undermined many a fledgling career already.
Any chances of trying to end this season at anything close to the power and ferocity with which he was swinging the bat in midsummer is long gone. How much first base he ends up playing in the future – or even picking up some right field – remains to be seen. And hopefully he will not need any sort of procedures or clean ups this offseason.

item.content:encoded:
Happy Tuesday, Camden Chatters!
Last night, we got a reprieve from the misery that has been Orioles baseball lately. And we got it mostly thanks to Pete Alonso (who else). Alonso hit his 39th and 40th home runs of the season last night, powering the Orioles to a 4-3 victory over the Blue Jays. He's now the 10th Oriole to have a 40-homer season, and his 108 RBI are the most in the American League. It's Alonso's first 40-homer season since 2023 and his fourth in his career.
Oh, and Alonso just happened to hit two homers on the day that his son, Teddy, celebrated his first birthday. What a guy.
Gunnar Henderson also homered, his 24th. Henderson had three hits in the game. Starting pitcher Shane Baz struggled through a three-run first inning, but went on to pitch 6.2 innings without allowing a run after the first. You can get the full details of the win in Alex Church's recap.
By my estimation, the Orioles have been out of the race since the Red Sox swept them in early September. Now it seems like the White Sox or Guardians will take the final Wild Card spot, with the other winning the AL Central. The Blue Jays are basically out of it as well, and the Orioles have the chance in this series to ensure their AL East foe is truly finished.
The Orioles won't go to the playoffs and they won't have a winning season, but they can put the nail in the coffin for the Blue Jays. And if the Orioles win tonight and tomorrow, these teams will leave Baltimore with the Blue Jays in last place instead of the Orioles. It's not something to get excited about, but it's always preferable to NOT be in last place.
Tonight, it'll be an old-man special as Chris Bassitt (37) and Max Scherzer (42) face off. It's a rematch of the game on 9/11, in which both pitchers went five innings. Scherzer allowed six runs and took the loss, while Bassitt allowed two runs and got the win. I wouldn't hate to see a repeat of that. The weather forecast today is pretty dicey, so hopefully they get the game in. I mean, I guess. Would it really matter if they didn't?
Links
How one swing exposed a season's worth of frustration for the Orioles – The Baltimore Banner
This was written about what happened after the Orioles lost on Sunday, but the contents have been a hot topic in Birdland. Specifically, how Craig Albernaz reacted to the press after Jeremiah Jackson grounded out on the first pitch against a struggling pitcher.
Alonso homers twice to reach 40 and give Orioles 4-3 win over Blue Jays – MASN Sports
Roch Kubatko's game story has plenty of quotes about how amazing Pete Alonso is, but also includes some info on Samuel Basallo, who exited last night's game after being hit square in the mask with a foul ball. Be ok, Samuel! Knocks to the head are scary.
Wehiwa Aloy and Joseph Dzierwa Named Orioles Minor League Player and Pitcher of the Year – MLB.com
The two awardees were at Camden Yards last night to accept, and both hopped into the broadcast booth to talk about their seasons. If you've never heard those two names spoken aloud before, here is your lesson. Wahiwa is pronounced Vuh-Hee-Vah. Dzierwa is pronounced Jer-Wah. Got it?
Birthdays and History
Is today your birthday? Happy birthday! You have a ton of Orioles birthday buddies, each more forgettable than the last. But because today is their birthday, today we remember them:
- Chris Ellis (34), eight games in 2021-22
- Luis García (51), six games in 2002
- César Devarez (57), 16 games in 1995-96.
- P.J. Forbes (59), nine games in 1998
- John Stefero (67), 61 games in 1983 and 1986
- Bob Harrison (b. 1930, d. 2023), two games in 1955-56
On this day in 1961, Jim Gentile hit his fifth grand slam of the year. That tied him with Ernie Banks for the most in a season. The current record is six, held by Travis Hafner and Don Mattingly.
In 1966, the Orioles clinched their first AL pennant with 6-1 victory over the Kansas City Athletics. Jim Palmer, just 20 years old, pitched a complete game.
In 1973, the Orioles defeated the Milwaukee Brewers 7-1 to clinch the division. Al Bumbry hit three triples in the win.
In 2012, the Orioles beat the Red Sox 9-6 in 13 innings, marking their 87th win of the year. They scored three runs in the top of the 13th with RBI hits from Jim Thome, Endy Chavez, and Manny Machado. Mark Reynolds and Adam Jones homered earlier. They remained one game out of the AL East after the Yankees pulled off an extra-innings win of their own.

item.content:encoded:
Pete Alonso’s second home run of the game and 40th of the season lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 comeback victory against the visiting Toronto Blue Jays in the opener of a three-game series Monday night.
Alonso’s two-run shot with two outs in the eighth inning gave Baltimore its first lead of the game. The Orioles pulled within 4 1/2 games of the White Sox in the race for the third American League wild card, while the Blue Jays now trail Chicago by 3 1/2 games.
Alonso also homered in the first inning and Gunnar Henderson (3-for-4) went deep in the sixth inning as the Orioles ended a three-game losing streak. Baltimore reliever Yennier Cano (4-3) worked 1 1/3 shutout innings, and Rico Garcia pitched a 1-2-3 ninth for his 10th save.
George Springer had two singles and an RBI for the Blue Jays, who lost for the fifth time in seven games. Tyler Rogers (2-3) gave up the decisive home run.
Tigers 9, Nationals 2
Ben Malgeri hit a three-run home run, Javier Baez and Spencer Torkelson each supplied two-run shots and host Detroit opened a three-game series with a romp over Washington.
River Ryan, elevated from Triple-A, started and pitched three scoreless innings while recording three strikeouts in his Tigers debut. Ryan, acquired in August from the Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal deal, last pitched in the majors in 2024. Keider Montero (10-9) followed with four shutout innings while striking out five.
Pinch hitter Yohandy Morales produced a two-run homer for the Nationals, who took their second loss in a row. DJ Herz (0-1) allowed four runs in four innings during his first major league outing since 2024.
Giants 5, Twins 2
Drew Gilbert homered, collected three hits and drove in a career-high-tying three runs as host San Francisco defeated Minnesota.
Brett Harris chipped in two hits, including a two-run single, as the Giants snapped a three-game losing streak. San Francisco reliever Tristan Beck (1-0) threw 2 2/3 innings of hitless ball, and Trent Harris tossed a perfect ninth inning for his second save.
Brooks Lee and Emmanuel Rodriguez homered for the Twins, who lost for the sixth time in nine games. Zebby Matthews (9-11) fanned nine in five innings but yielded five runs on eight hits.
–Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
When you are as bush league an operation as Craig Albernaz’s 2026 Baltimore Orioles, it usually doesn’t take long for your complete lack of fundamentals and remedial-at-best baseball IQ to shine through.
Monday night, starting pitcher Shane Baz issued a leadoff walk on a pitch timer violation, then gave up three runs on three straight pitchers, continuing his ability to focus and command in the first inning, and these baseball losers were on the cusp of clinching yet another losing season under baseball failure exec Mike Elias. Thanks to Pete Alonso they staved off loss No. 82 – don’t worry, it’s coming – and won game No. 75 (they’re better than last year!) in a 4-3 victory over Toronto at a predictably desolate Camden Yards.
Alonso hit an opposite field homer early in the game and Gunnar Henderson delivered a solo homer and Alonso won it for them by clubbing homer No. 40 to left field, a two-run shot that gave them a rare one-run victory. Problem is they are 4.5 games back in the Wild Card and they have five to play, so you do the math.
“Just really stoked I was able to come through for the team right there,” Alonso said on the MASN post-game show.
Baz – as utterly middling of an MLB starter as you will fine who Elias mortgaged what was left of his middling farm system for at the time – showed guts, getting over his poor first inning (that’s been a constant) – and performed well after taking a liner off his elbow last time out. There is a good chance that this trade haunts this organization with 21-year old catcher Caden Bodine already on the Rays taxi squad, but Elias is a human curse so we’ve come to expect no less
So Close To Finally Being Over
Outside of Alonso, hasn’t been much to come to the park to see, yet again, this season. (Rookie catcher Samuel Basallo was for a while but is clearly beat up and getting checked for a concussion after taking a hard foul tip behind the plate Monday).
And with Elias and Albernaz coming back, you can already smell the stench of their 2027 season before it starts, and the propaganda campaign to whitewash this season and try to grift you into spending on next year’s model is well under way.
Does anyone get excited about a team that can catch or run or throw? Do you enjoy watching AAA players all over the place nine years into a rebuild? Let me guess, Albernaz now pretending that getting tough about mistakes made by guys like Rece Hinds and Jeremiah Jackson – who have no business being in MLB, but Elias is so inexplicably horrible at his job they are – doesn’t do it for you?
No problem, MASN went to great lengths Monday to gaslight you about this lost season, and the bumbling clown running the dugout. They run interference and peddle fake talking points about what Henderson has become, pretending he hasn’t tanked as bad as Adley Rutschman did here, and cover for his constant misstep in all aspects of play … And now all of a sudden they’re championing Albernaz’s pathetic rants, 150 games into a lost year, about guys who don’t belong here and are riffing on what a tone he is setting by castrating career minor leaguers.
You aren’t fooling anybody, just demeaning yourselves. Yuck.
Just when you thought you couldn’t lose any more respect for an absolute joke of a franchise, they go and surprise you again by taking their overt PR campaign to another level. There is no bottom with these people and how low they are willing to sink for their paychecks. They all deserve each other. Baltimore deserves so much more.
